reading: The corner pattern is completed to four-fold symmetry about the grid centre, and each outer ring side is drawn as a dotted line (every second cell) in the colour of the mark next to the corner, running from corner to corner.

slots.pattern: the marks in one corner of the input
slots.dotted_line: between each pair of mirrored outer corner marks, period 2, colour of the mark adjacent to the corner on that side

why: output is symmetric about both central axes and each outer side is a period-2 run between its two corners

reading: Missing parts of a symmetric pattern are filled so the output is symmetric about the grid's central axes.
why: output is symmetric (horizontal, vertical and diagonal) about the grid centre and contains every input fg cell

reading: The big rectangle extends each of its rows and columns outward to the grid border in all four directions, except rows/columns that contain a marker on that side, which are not extended at all.

slots.directions: up, down, left, right to the border
slots.blocked: a row/column on a given side is skipped entirely if any marker lies on it on that side

why: every unblocked rectangle row/column is filled to the border; blocked ones stay empty

reading: A background cell that is the centre of a plus formed by four dominoes (two cells at distance 2-3 in each of the four directions) becomes 4.

new_rows.name: plus_centre
new_rows.datalog:
fgat(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
plus_centre(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C0), !fgat(Y, X), Y1 = Y - 2, Y2 = Y - 3, fgat(Y1, X), fgat(Y2, X), Y3 = Y + 2, Y4 = Y + 3, fgat(Y3, X), fgat(Y4, X), X1 = X - 2, X2 = X - 3, fgat(Y, X1), fgat(Y, X2), X3 = X + 2, X4 = X + 3, fgat(Y, X3), fgat(Y, X4).

why: exactly the plus-centre cells become colour 4; nothing else changes

reading: The 6-line with a 2 at its head points a ray from the 2 through the 7 area; the first frame cell (non-7) the ray hits becomes 7.

slots.pointer: the 6 run ending in the 2 cell (direction 6 -> 2, may be diagonal)
slots.hit: first non-7 cell on the ray

why: only the first non-7 cell along the pointer's direction changes, to 7
invariants: all cells except the hit cell

reading: Every 2 lying inside the bounding box of a 3-block gets a ring of 1s on all eight neighbours (overwriting 3, 0 or outside 2s); 2s outside the blocks are untouched.

new_rows.name: ring2
new_rows.datalog:
b3(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), px(Y, X, 3).
top(O, min(Y)) :- b3(O), obj(O, Y, X).
bot(O, max(Y)) :- b3(O), obj(O, Y, X).
lft(O, min(X)) :- b3(O), obj(O, Y, X).
rgt(O, max(X)) :- b3(O), obj(O, Y, X).
in2(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 2), top(O, T), bot(O, B), lft(O, L), rgt(O, R), Y >= T, Y <= B, X >= L, X <= R.
ring2(Y, X) :- in2(Y0, X0), off(DY, DX), Y = Y0 + DY, X = X0 + DX, px(Y, X, C), !in2(Y, X).

why: all 8-neighbours of in-block 2s (except in-block 2s) become 1; nothing else changes
invariants: 2s outside blocks not adjacent to in-block 2s

reading: In a lattice of identical small tiles, when two tiles in the same tile-row or tile-column carry the same odd colour at the same position, every tile between them gets that colour at that position.

slots.odd_cell: a tile cell whose colour differs from the usual colour at that position
slots.pair: two tiles on one tile-row or tile-column with the same odd colour at the same position
slots.fill: that position in every tile between them takes the odd colour

why: for each position, odd colours form unbroken runs between matching tiles along tile-rows/columns

reading: The bottom row and right column are colour keys; each interior cell whose column key equals its row key takes that colour, forming coloured blocks on the diagonal.

slots.column_key: colour of the bottom-row cell in that column
slots.row_key: colour of the right-column cell in that row
slots.rule: cell (Y,X) gets colour C when both keys equal C

why: a cell is coloured C exactly when bottom[X] = right[Y] = C

reading: The input is repeated twice side by side.
why: output is a 1x2 row of input copies

reading: The input is tiled N x N times, where N is the number of distinct colours in the input.

new_rows.name: colour_reps
new_rows.datalog:
crow(C, min(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
ccol(C, min(X)) :- crow(C, Y), px(Y, X, C).
colour_reps(Y, X) :- crow(C, Y), ccol(C, X).

slots.extent: count of colour_reps cells (one cell per distinct colour) = N, giving an N x N block of copies

why: every block of the N x N output is the input, N = number of distinct colours
